Competitors were assessed by 8 judges who each awarded a score in a range from 0–10.
The judges were numbered 0–7. The competitors’ names are stored in the one-dimensional
array , and their scores are stored in the two-dimensional array (see Figure 1).

SCORES[1][4]
(a) State the judge who awarded the highest score to the competitor Tea Fox. [1]
The highest attainable score in gymnastics is 10.0 .
(b) Construct an algorithm that determines and outputs the number of times the highest
attainable score was awarded in this competition. [4]
A competitor’s final score is calculated by ignoring the highest and the lowest mark awarded
and averaging the remaining marks.
For example, the highest mark awarded to Lilly Bush was 7.9, and the lowest mark was 6.9,
so her final score was (7.2 + 6.9 + 6.9 + 6.9 + 6.9 + 7.2) / 6.
(c) Construct an algorithm in pseudocode to output the name and the final score for
every competitor. [10]
